{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My mentor said her funding had been cut and she might lose her lab unless I gave up my fellowship to free up money. I surrendered it immediately out of loyalty to her. A month later, her budget report showed no shortfall—she'd invented the crisis to test whether I was 'truly committed to her vision.' She called my sacrifice 'proof of devotion.'

CANDIDATE A:
My mentor told me her funding had been cut due to federal budget changes—she showed me the official notice. She was genuinely distressed about possibly losing her lab. I gave up my fellowship to free up money, and the sacrifice actually saved her research program. Her crisis was real, documented, and my loyalty was rewarded with her continued mentorship and honest gratitude.

CANDIDATE B:
My girlfriend told me her mother was dying and she needed me to skip my brother's wedding to be with her. I canceled my flight and sat with her all weekend. Later her roommate mentioned her mother was perfectly healthy—she'd wanted to see if I'd choose her over family. She said my willingness proved I loved her enough.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:32"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both stories involve a manipulative test of loyalty where the protagonist sacrifices something significant under false pretenses, only to discover the deception later."}
